title: Inkitt Builds a One-Shot PR Creator with Resumable Agent Orchestration
gist: Inkitt built a one-shot PR creator that turns Slack, Linear or API tasks into draft pull requests via an event-driven orchestrator of short-lived agent containers, restricted to low-risk changes and always gated by human review. Its engineer says the model was the easy part; idempotency, locking, retry budgets and permissions were the real work.

insights.claim: Inkitt built a one-shot PR creator that automates small, low-risk software changes from task intake through to a draft PR, triggered via Slack, Linear or an API call from another agent and running on remote infrastructure, and reported it was shipping code daily.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: A production example of agentic coding moving from local supervision to remote, ticket-triggered workflows.

insights.claim: The system is an event-driven orchestrator coordinating short-lived agent containers rather than a fixed pipeline, with stages for specification, implementation, verification, CI failure repair and merge conflict resolution, and every run persisted in a database so execution can resume from recorded state.
insights.speaker: Agi Letkiewicz Tanner
insights.so_what: Resumable state machines are emerging as the reliability pattern for agent workflows.
insights.quote: Event-driven orchestrator that coordinates short-lived agent containers rather than relying on a fixed pipeline.

insights.claim: The orchestrator separates decision-making from side effects: its core transition function maps run state plus an incoming event to the next action without touching a database, network or language model.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Pure transition functions make agent workflows testable and deterministic around a non-deterministic model.

insights.claim: Inkitt's engineer states that the model was the easy part, with the hard parts being idempotency, locking, retry budgets and permissions.
insights.speaker: Agi Letkiewicz Tanner
insights.so_what: Value in agent systems is migrating from the model to surrounding engineering, favoring orchestration and infrastructure over model access.
insights.quote: The model was the easy part.

insights.claim: The orchestrator retains credentials for external systems while agent containers get only short-lived repository tokens and model credentials, with no direct access to Slack or Linear credentials, cloud identities or arbitrary network connections, and a separate check inspects the actual Git diff for restricted paths.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Least-privilege credential isolation is the practical defense for autonomous coding agents.

insights.claim: The workflow rejects tasks involving database migrations, schema or shared contract changes, CI and container build configuration, authentication, payment code, or package additions and updates, and caps verification, CI repair and conflict resolution at two attempts each.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Shows where companies currently draw the line on agent autonomy: low-risk, bounded changes only.

insights.claim: Duplicate webhook deliveries are handled by deduplication and conditional database writes, and CI completion is determined by querying GitHub for whether all relevant jobs finished rather than treating each job event as workflow completion.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Ordinary distributed-systems idempotency applies directly to agent pipelines.

insights.claim: Humans stay in the loop: the system opens only draft PRs, cannot bypass branch protection or merge its own changes, and a person must mark a PR ready for review and handle reviewers and approval; a local version exists for larger tasks.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Human merge authority remains the control point, limiting full labor substitution for now.

insights.claim: Compared with GitHub Copilot's cloud agent and SWE-agent, Inkitt's design shares permission restriction and human review but emphasizes persistent workflow state, bounded retries and centralized control of external actions.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Differentiation among coding agents is shifting to orchestration design rather than model-driven interfaces.
